name: The Ephesians who burned their books
charge: Confessing and shewing their deeds, and burning fifty thousand pieces of silver worth of curious arts before all men
summary: After the seven sons of Sceva were overcome by the man they tried to exorcise, this was known to all the Jews and Greeks dwelling at Ephesus, and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified. Many that believed came and confessed and showed their deeds, and many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together and burned them before all men. They counted the price and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver. So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.
offenseFull: Paul had come to Ephesus and gone into the synagogue and spoken boldly for three months, and then separated the disciples and disputed daily in the school of one Tyrannus, and this continued by the space of two years, so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks (Acts 19:8-10). The Jews are the southern kingdom and the Greeks are the Greek-speaking of our nation, the northern; that is who the Ephesians are, Israelites dwelling at Ephesus. That is also how Colosse heard it, though there is no verse saying Paul ever went to Colosse; look at the map and see how close it sits to Ephesus, and there is the precept for it. And what they were being turned from is named in the same chapter: not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul had persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods which are made with hands, and the temple of the great goddess Diana was in danger of being despised, whom all Asia and the world worshipped (Acts 19:26-27). Ephesus was a city given to the worship of a female deity, the fertility goddess whose small images were sold in every street and whose trade fed the silversmiths; that is why Demetrius could raise the craftsmen, and why the city cried out about the space of two hours in the theatre, Great is Diana of the Ephesians (Acts 19:24-25, Acts 19:34). Our brothers have stood in those ruins and seen what the place was.

Then came the defeat of the vagabond exorcists, and it was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus, and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified (Acts 19:17). Many that believed came and confessed and showed their deeds; and many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together and burned them before all men, and they counted the price of them and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver (Acts 19:18-19). Curious arts are the magical arts and jugglery practised by the conjurers of that city, and that is witchcraft by another name, the very thing the law forbids: no diviner, no observer of times, no enchanter, no witch, no charmer, no consulter with familiar spirits, no wizard, no necromancer, and no witch suffered to live (Deuteronomy 18:10-12, Exodus 22:18). Witchcraft is still named among the works of the flesh in the letters, so it did not stop being real in the New Testament (Galatians 5:19-20). Notice also that they came and confessed and showed their deeds, which no man does unless the law still stands and he knows what he has broken. The confession was made in the open, and the instruments of the old practice went into the fire in front of the same people. They burned their own books, and they did not sell them first.
judgmentFull: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed (Acts 19:20). The gain counted in the record is not the money given up but the growth of the word in that city, and from that city into all Asia. The spirit was so heavy in Ephesus that places Paul never physically walked into were touched by it, and a congregation rose at Colosse that had never seen his face (Colossians 1:1-6, Colossians 2:1). Some of the instruction written back to that region reads differently once the goddess is known: the charge that the women keep silence in the congregation went to a people repenting out of a religion built on female power and woman worship, which is the same doctrine under new names today (1 Corinthians 14:34-35).

The turning did not end the watch. Paul later called the elders of that same church and warned them that after his departing grievous wolves would enter in among them, not sparing the flock, and that of their own selves men would arise speaking perverse things to draw away disciples after them, and told them to watch and remember that by the space of three years he ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears (Acts 20:29-31). What is burned can be replaced by another corruption under a better name, and the men who had made the fire were the ones told to watch.

text.text: And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:

So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.
For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.
But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.
Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch,
Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.
For all that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord: and because of these abominations the Lord thy God doth drive them out from before thee.
Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.
Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness,
Idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies,
So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.
Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timotheus our brother,
To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you,
Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love which ye have to all the saints,
For the hope which is laid up for you in heaven, whereof ye heard before in the word of the truth of the gospel;
Which is come unto you, as it is in all the world; and bringeth forth fruit, as it doth also in you, since the day ye heard of it, and knew the grace of God in truth:
For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;
Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law.
And if they will learn any thing, let them ask their husbands at home: for it is a shame for women to speak in the church.
For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.

The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.
Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it: but thou shalt utterly detest it, and thou shalt utterly abhor it; for it is a cursed thing.
